text.p: *Australian bond futures contracts remained around Monday's weaker levels in after-hours trading as U.S. Treasuries extended Friday's massive sell-off.
*First leg of U.S. refunding starts later on Tuesday.
Australian bond futures contracts remained around Monday's weaker levels in after-hours trading as U.S. Treasuries extended Friday's massive sell-off.
The September 10-year bond contract ended SYCOM at 93.525, down from Monday's dayside close of 93.545, but again found support around the 93.510 area.

The market gets back into full swing after Monday's New South Wales state holiday, although much of the sting has been taken out of the reaction to the sharp, pre-weekend U.S. sell-off due to yesterday's illiquid trading.

However, analysts said that downside pressures could build up if the contract enters a broad support area between 93.370 to 93.470, although on the day it looks set to trade in a 93.500 to 93.550 range.

U.S. Treasuries continued to correct last week's rally and remained under a cloud after Friday's huge sell-off, which was triggered by stronger than expected non-farm payrolls and data showing a more buoyant manufacturing sector.
The U.S. faces the first of three quarterly refunding auctions later on Tuesday when US$16.0 billion of three-year notes will be offered.
